Actions.Label: Have a proper chat
Say: Grandma says my posture is terrible. I told her I'm a professional athlete. She said that explains it.
George has been sitting outside more often. He says the sun is good for his joints. I think he likes watching the birds.
I ran the long way around the river this morning. Came back tired and in a better mood. Annoying how that works.
People hear I play gridball and decide they know my whole personality. I let them. It's easier than correcting everybody.
I used to think I had to win every time. Now I just want to play a game where nobody gets hurt and the grass is dry.
Sam has been writing new songs. She says I should be in the music video. I said only if I get a stunt double.
I keep a football under the bed. It doesn't fit. I keep it there anyway.
Grandma made cookies for the whole town. George claimed he didn't want one. I saw him take three.
The beach is good for running when the sand is firm. When it's soft, it's good for regretting your choices.
I've been trying to read more. The first page is easy. The second page is where my brain goes looking for a ball.
Leah says my sketches look like somebody kicked a notebook down the stairs. I said that's movement.
Sometimes I miss being a kid who could play all afternoon and not think about what came next.
I don't like talking about my parents. I don't mind talking about Grandma. That's probably not the same thing.
Vincent wants me to teach him a trick with the ball. I told him to start with catching it. He said that's boring.
There's a bench by the ice cream stand where you can see the whole beach. I sit there after practice sometimes.
I bought new shoes. They look fast. I haven't tested them yet because I'm worried they'll be faster than me.
George called me by my dad's name this morning. He apologized. I told him it was fine. It was, mostly.
I like helping with the farm chores. It's exercise, but nobody asks me to keep score.
Caroline says I was always loud as a child. I said I was enthusiastic. She said those aren't mutually exclusive.
There's a town game coming up. I might enter. Not for the prize. I like having something to train for.
I've been keeping a notebook of plays. Most of them are terrible. I draw them anyway.
Some people think being strong means never asking for help. That's a very inconvenient definition.
Sam says I should learn to play guitar. I said my fingers are already busy. She said that's not how fingers work.
The farm dog has learned to bring me a stick. I throw it. The dog wins. We have an understanding.
I like when somebody watches a game without shouting advice. It makes the whole field feel bigger.

Steps.Narrate: Alex is standing near the tide line with a scuffed football tucked under one arm. She nudges it back with her foot when it rolls away.

Steps.Say: I come here when the field gets too crowded. The beach doesn't care how many goals you scored last week.
I used to practise until my legs gave out. My grandmother would call me in and I'd pretend I couldn't hear her.
Now I can hear her. I just don't always know when to stop. That's an improvement, apparently.
I've been thinking about entering the spring tournament. Not because I expect to win. I want to see what I can do without making it my whole life.
Would you help me practise? I need somebody who won't cheer every time I manage to kick the ball straight.
Passing. Right. We can do that. It sounds boring, which probably means it's useful.

Options.Label: Try a full match and see what happens.

Steps.Say: You want to get tackled in the sand? Fine. But I'm blaming you when we both get sand in our shoes.

Options.Label: Take a break and talk first.

Steps.Say: That's... actually nice. I thought you'd tell me to run laps. We can sit for a minute.
That was good. Not the practice. The part where nobody needed me to be the best one on the beach.

Actions.Label: The old photograph
Actions.Conditions: Fouky.CharacterInteract_HAS_FLAG Ch1_{{NpcName}}, PLAYER_HEARTS Current {{NpcName}} 4, Fouky.CharacterInteract_COUNTER Talks_{{NpcName}} 6, !Fouky.CharacterInteract_HAS_FLAG Ch2_{{NpcName}}

Steps.Narrate: Alex has a photograph balanced on her knee at the porch steps. Evelyn's handwriting is visible on the back.

Steps.Say: This is my parents. I don't show it much. People look at it and start asking questions, and then I have to decide how much truth fits in a conversation.
Grandma keeps it in the family album. I took it out because I wanted to remember the day, not the way everything ended.
I was little. I remember the picnic blanket, the red cooler, and my dad trying to catch a ball with one hand while holding a plate.
George doesn't talk about them much. Sometimes he starts, then stops. I don't push. I know what that feels like.
I thought maybe I could put the photograph somewhere I can see it without having to explain it.

Options.Label: By the window, where the light reaches it.

Steps.Say: Yeah. Somewhere ordinary. Not hidden in a box, not displayed like an announcement.

Options.Label: Keep it in the album until you're ready.

Steps.Say: That's fair. I don't have to decide today. I can put it back and still have looked at it.

Options.Label: Ask Evelyn where she'd like it.

Steps.Say: She'll say wherever I want. Then she'll bring out the good frame. I know her.
Thanks. I didn't need you to say anything about them. I just needed somebody to look at the picture with me.

Actions.Label: A game without a score
Actions.Conditions: Fouky.CharacterInteract_HAS_FLAG Ch2_{{NpcName}}, PLAYER_HEARTS Current {{NpcName}} 6, Fouky.CharacterInteract_COUNTER Talks_{{NpcName}} 10, !Fouky.CharacterInteract_HAS_FLAG Ch3_{{NpcName}}

Steps.Narrate: The field is empty. Alex has set two water bottles by the fence and drawn a line in the dirt with her shoe.

Steps.Say: I asked a few people to come practise. Then I changed my mind. Too many opinions, too many people keeping score.
I want to play for an hour and stop when I'm tired. Not when somebody says I should be better.
That sounds like a small thing. It isn't, for me. I have a habit of turning every good day into a test.
Grandma said I should learn to enjoy the game again. She says it while handing me a sandwich, so I can't argue.
I want to try it today. Just pass the ball, miss a few, laugh, and go home.

Options.Label: Pass until the sun goes down.

Steps.Say: Okay. But if I start counting, call me out. I want this to be a game, not a spreadsheet.
Now we're talking. Three points for a backwards kick? Five for hitting the fence? This is going to be terrible.

Options.Label: Sit here and watch the clouds.

Steps.Say: That's not football. ...Maybe that's the point. I can do that for a while.
I forgot what time it was. That's probably the best practice I've had in months.
